Q: RuntimeError: Failed to import transformers ('NoneType' object has no attribute 'split') with Python 3.11, TensorFlow 2.15 & Docker A:

Headline: Fixed RuntimeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'split' by using NVIDIA CUDA Base Image and Multi-Stage Build

I found the solution. The issue was that the transformers library (specifically the modeling_auto module) was attempting to list or parse CUDA device environment variables that were missing or incorrectly initialized in the standard python:3.11-slim Docker image.

The fix required moving from a generic Python image to an official NVIDIA CUDA runtime image and ensuring the environment was correctly mapped.

The Solution

1. Host Preparation

On the Windows host, ensure WSL2 is installed and Docker Desktop -> Settings -> Resources -> WSL Integration is enabled for your distribution (e.g., Ubuntu).

2. Optimized Multi-Stage Dockerfile

By using nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-cudnn8-runtime-ubuntu22.04 as the base, we provide the system-level drivers that transformers expects.

Dockerfile

# Stage 1: Builder
FROM nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-cudnn8-runtime-ubuntu22.04 as builder

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install Python 3.11 and build tools
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    python3.11 \
    python3.11-dev \
    python3.11-venv \
    build-essential \
    gcc \
    wget \
    curl \
    git \
    libffi-dev \
    libssl-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Setup Virtual Environment to isolate dependencies
RUN python3.11 -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Stage 2: Runtime
FROM nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-cudnn8-runtime-ubuntu22.04 as runtime

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
# Crucial: Map the venv path to the new container's environment
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"

# Copy only the compiled venv from builder
COPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv

WORKDIR /app
COPY . .

CMD ["python", "grpc_server.py"]

Why this fixes the error:

  • Environment Parity: The transformers library scans for CUDA capabilities during import. In a slim Python image, it fails silently or returns None for certain device queries, causing the .split() method to crash. The NVIDIA base image provides the necessary libraries (.so files) to handle these queries.

  • Path Consistency: Explicitly defining the PATH for the virtual environment ensures that sentence_transformers finds the correct transformers version without interference from system-level Python stubs.
